newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ's Clark says Birch RBNZ comments extraordinary.
newsitem.headline: NZ's Clark says Birch RBNZ comments extraordinary.

text.p: New Zealand Labour leader Helen Clark said on Monday it was "extraordinary" for Finance Minister Bill Birch to indicate that the central bank's 0-2 percent inflation target may be negotiable in coalition talks.

Birch told Reuters Financial Television that a loosening of the target "may well be" on the agenda for coalition talks between the caretaker National Party government and nationalist New Zealand First, which holds the balance of power after the inconclusive general election.
Asked if Birch was trying to cut the ground from under the feet of Labour, which favours a wider target band of minus one to three percent, Clark said: "I find Mr Birch's statement extraordinary."

She told reporters: "This is the man who has for six years defended that target absolutely rigidly, abused Labour when we announced a reasonable policy of broadening the range. Now he will say anything, be prepared to trade anything to get some sort of agreement to keep him in power. It really is incredible."

Clark was speaking after a Labour party caucus which she said held a general discussion on coalition options. Labour could form a centre-left government if it can reach agreement with New Zealand First and the left-wing Alliance.
Clark said Labour had formed its negotiating team, which would hold a preliminary discussion later on Monday.
